ig_carousel_topic.topic: Public money vs. sharp money: how to tell which is moving the line
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text: Is the line moving because the public is on it, or because the sharps are?
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text: Most bettors assume a line moves because everyone is piling on. That's often wrong. A line can move on 15% of the ticket count if that 15% is big money from professional accounts.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text: The tell is ticket count vs. money percentage. If 70% of tickets are on the favorite but the line moves toward the underdog, sharp money is on the dog. The books are pricing out the professionals, not the crowd.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text: Example: Team A opens -3. By tip, 68% of public tickets are on Team A. Line moves to -2.5. That reverse movement means sportsbooks took enough sharp action on the +3 side to shade the number back. The public didn't move it.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text: Ticket count tells you what the crowd thinks. Line movement tells you what the books fear. Those two things disagree more often than you'd expect.
